title: Sales Enablement Unified Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's core positioning and messaging, competitive battlecards, pitch-deck guidance, pricing guidance and negotiation levers, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Use this document as the canonical sales enablement reference for pre-sales, solutions, and AE teams.

1) One-line and elevator pitches
- One-line: Redwood Inference is a production-first LLM inference platform that delivers predictable latency, lower unit costs, and flexible deployment across hosted, dedicated, and private environments.
- 30s elevator: Teams choose Redwood when they need consistent, production-grade LLM inference that scales across hosted APIs, reserved GPU capacity, and private deployments. We combine a GPU-optimized serving runtime, smart routing and caching, and observability tooling so engineering teams can ship LLM features with predictable latency, lower token costs, and enterprise controls.

2) Target personas & top buyer problems
- Personas:
  - ML/ML infra engineers: need predictable latency, model versioning, and low variance throughput for product integrations.
  - Platform/Infra leads: require capacity planning, cost visibility, and centralized runtime for multiple teams.
  - Product/Engineering managers: care about time-to-market and consistent UX.
  - Security/Compliance/Risk: need controls, proofs (SOC2, audit logs), and data residency.

- Top buyer problems we solve:
  - Unpredictable latency and tail latency issues in production LLM workloads.
  - High per-token unit cost and lack of batching/caching optimizations.
  - Operational blind spots: poor tracing, no per-route cost data, and ad-hoc rollouts.
  - Compliance and data residency constraints for regulated industries.

3) Core value propositions (by persona)
- ML Engineer: Reduced inference cost (batching + cache) and predictable latencies with native KV cache and kernel selection.
- Platform Lead: Unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private with autoscaling and SLA-backed capacity.
- Security & Compliance: Private control plane options, KMS integrations, audit logs and enterprise SLAs.
- Product Manager: Fast iteration via consistent API and built-in rollout/A-B tooling.

4) Key proof points and differentiators (short bullets for pitch)
- Production-first: pre-built observability (per-route latency/cost), built-in rollouts and regression alerts.
- Cost controls: intelligent batching, cache hints and quantization recommendations reduce unit cost by 20-50% in reference workloads.
- Deployment flexibility: same API for hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem).
- Reliability: automated fallback routing to compatible model variants and regional failover.

5) Competitive brief / battlecards (quick reference)
- Competitors covered: OpenAI (hosted LLM API), Anthropic, Google Vertex AI, Cloud GPU providers / self-hosted runtimes, Specialized inference vendors (e.g., Hugging Face Infinity, Run:ai).

- Redwood vs OpenAI / Anthropic:
  - Strengths: More deployment flexibility (dedicated & private), better cost controls for production workloads (batching, caching, quantized model recommendations), and deeper observability for SLO-driven teams.
  - Weaknesses: Fewer proprietary cutting-edge LLM model releases; customers focused solely on point-in-time generative quality comparisons may prefer first access providers.
  - Recommended messaging: "If you care primarily about production economics, observability, and enterprise controls — not just early model access — Redwood is the lower-risk, lower-cost path to production LLMs."

- Redwood vs Google Vertex / Cloud GPU endpoints:
  - Strengths: Opinionated runtime optimizations for LLMs, built-in quality guardrails and rollout tooling, simpler integration (single API across environments).
  - Weaknesses: Cloud providers may have deeper cloud-native integrations; leverage partnerships for customers needing native cloud billing.

- Redwood vs Self-hosted runtimes / in-house inference:
  - Strengths: Faster time-to-production, operational savings (we manage complex batching/serve heuristics), and lower total-cost-of-ownership for teams that frequently tune for latency/cost.
  - Weaknesses: For teams who already have a large infra investment and staff to run inference, the OPEX calculus may favor in-house. Focus rebuttal on long tail costs: SRE/observability/tooling and continuous model upgrades.

- Battlecard quick rebuttals (top objections):
  - "We can just run our own GPUs": "Most teams underestimate ongoing tuning and edge-case ops; Redwood's runtime and telemetry reduce SRE time and deliver consistent unit cost improvements backed by observable metrics."
  - "We need the absolute best-performing model": "Redwood supports market-leading open models and provides model-onboarding/rollout tooling so you can validate and pin model versions—while ensuring production SLAs."

6) Recommended pitch deck (10-12 slides)
1. Title / Hook: customer problem statement (latency/cost/ops)
2. Vision & Value Prop: Redwood's promise (production economics + deployment flexibility)
3. How it works (high-level): serving runtime, routing, caching, deployment modes
4. Product demo / screenshot: console dashboards, tracing, rollout UI, per-route cost view
5. Performance & cost benchmarks: latency P50/P95, tokens/ms, typical cost delta vs naive API
6. Security & compliance: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private deploy
7. Case study: metrics and ROI (see examples below)
8. Pricing overview & commitment options
9. Migration / onboarding plan: POC -> pilot -> production rollout
10. Commercial / success model: support SLAs, playbook for adoption
11. FAQ & next steps
12. Appendix: model catalog, quantization profiles, technical architecture

7) Pricing guidance & negotiation levers
- High-level packaging:
  - Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation and embedding pricing; recommended entry-level for SMBs and early proofs.
  - Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual committed GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower per-token costs.
  - Redwood Private (license + support): enterprise licensing and on-prem/VPC deployments for regulated workloads.

- Example indicative commercial ranges (reference only; always consult pricing team):
  - Hosted API: $0.0006-0.015 per generated token depending on model family and throughput.
  - Dedicated: committed monthly $20k-200k+ based on GPU type and concurrency.
  - Private: license + integration/support fees; typically multi-year engagements.

- Discount & negotiation levers:
  - Commit term: multi-year or annual commit discounts, ramp schedules.
  - Usage tiers: stronger discounts at high monthly token volumes.
  - Feature bundles: observability retention, premium SLAs, compliance add-ons (e.g., HIPAA) as upsell items.
  - Proof-of-value: reduced pricing during pilot with clearly defined success criteria and rollout plan.

- Commercial play suggestions:
  - SMB / Mid-market: start on hosted API + quickstart templates; upsell Dedicated when steady-state usage is predictable.
  - Enterprise / Regulated: propose a pilot on Dedicated or Private with built-in migration & security review, delivered in partnership with solutions engineering.

8) Representative case studies (1-page summaries, anonymized where required)
- Case study: ChatOps SaaS (SaaS company, ~50M monthly active users)
  - Problem: Tail latency and high per-request cost on user-facing chat feature; inconsistent service during peak.
  - Solution: Migrated to Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling and prefix caching; added quantization profile for production model.
  - Results: P95 latency reduced from 1,200ms -> 420ms; token cost reduced by ~37% in steady-state; error rate stable during 2x traffic peaks.
  - Timeline: 8-week pilot -> 6-week production rollout.
  - Ownership: Solutions engineering + customer platform team.

- Case study: FinReg (regulated fintech)
  - Problem: Data residency and audit requirements prevented use of public hosted APIs.
  - Solution: Deployed Redwood Private (VPC) with customer-managed KMS and audit logging; implemented RBAC and integration with on-prem ingest.
  - Results: Achieved SOC2 compliance evidence for inference pipeline; accelerated model-backed product launch by 3 months vs internal build.

9) Security FAQ for prospects (concise, shareable answers)
- Q: Where is customer data stored and how long is it retained?
  - A: For Hosted customers, data residency is selectable by region; logs and payloads retention defaults to 30 days (configurable). For Dedicated and Private, telemetry and logs can be routed to customer-owned storage per contract.

- Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
  - A: Yes. We integrate with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and support HSM-backed keys for Private deployments.

- Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
  - A: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified. For enterprise deals we provide compliance evidence packages and will coordinate SOC2 report sharing under NDA. We also provide artifacts for ISO/IEC readiness conversations.

- Q: How is data encrypted in transit and at rest?
  - A: All network traffic to hosted endpoints is TLS 1.2+; data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 by default. Private deployments follow customer-specified encryption policies.

- Q: How do you handle model privacy and PII?
  - A: Customers can elect not to persist training or telemetry payloads; Redwood offers redaction hooks, PII detection in prompt pre-process and configurable retention policies.

- Q: Can I run Redwood in my VPC / on-prem?
  - A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC peering, private control plane options, and an on-prem package for air-gapped requirements.

- Q: Do you offer penetration testing and third-party audits?
  - A: Yes. We run annual pen tests and external audit cycles; redacted summaries and remediation plans can be shared during procurement cycles.

- Q: How are access and RBAC handled?
  - A: RBAC with SSO integrations (OIDC/SAML), per-user roles, and token-scoped API keys. Audit logs capture administrative actions and config changes.

- Q: What are data deletion and export policies?
  - A: Customers can request data export or deletion; APIs and support processes exist to remove customer data from hosted systems within contractual SLAs.

10) Objection handling & rebuttals (concise)
- "Your unit costs are higher than self-hosted": "Total cost of ownership usually favors Redwood for teams that need production SLAs, observability, and ongoing model tuning. Our Optimize tooling often reduces per-token costs materially."
- "We need to own the data": "Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC endpoints gives full control over network boundaries and key management; we will map controls required during pre-sales security review."
- "We already use a cloud provider endpoint": "Redwood complements cloud endpoints by offering a unified runtime and ops tooling across multi-cloud/private environments; this simplifies governance for platform teams."
